audit_findings.title: The completed acquisitions make the earnings numerator and balance-sheet perimeter incoherent
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.516 billion acquisition cash outflow; $2.0 billion new notes with $117.5 million computed annual coupon interest, equal to 25.4% of the $462.4 million anchor OE; acquired businesses contributed $320.287 million of partial-period sales and $24.625 million of partial-period pretax earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: The DCF capitalizes pre-acquisition OE while the cash and debt bridge reflects the post-acquisition company. Excluding acquired earnings understates OE, while excluding the associated full interest burden overstates OE; omitted acquired claims could also overstate the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: To the extent we finance such acquisitions with additional debt, the incurrence of such debt may result in a significant increase in our interest expense and financial leverage, which could be further exacerbated by volatility in the debt capital markets.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a future acquisition risk. Both acquisitions closed in December 2025 and are reflected in the May 2026 balance sheet and partial-period results. The opposing numerator effects prevent determining the net value direction, but the $117.5 million annual coupon alone is large relative to anchor OE and is reasonably capable of changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE and the bridge on one post-acquisition date using filed results for Foley and CP&P, a full-run-rate interest charge, and all acquired liabilities, leases, contingent consideration, NCI and other senior claims; then rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: FY2024 OE may capitalize an unusually large government subsidy as recurring earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $69.4 million pretax, equal to 15.0% of $462.4 million anchor OE; compared with $13.8 million in FY2023, $48.1 million in the first nine months of FY2025 and $36.0 million in the first nine months of FY2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Government assistance reduced cost of goods sold and therefore increased the earnings base that can enter OE and be capitalized through the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The government assistance recognized under the programs during 2024 was $69.4 million, compared to $13.8 million of government assistance recognized in 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The subsidy was demonstrably included in reported FY2024 earnings, but the record does not establish whether the OE schedule removed or normalized it. Continued assistance in 2025 and 2026 shows that zero recurrence is not established; nevertheless, the FY2024 amount was five times FY2023 and represents 15% of anchor OE, making incorrect capitalization reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $69.4 million through the FY2024 OE reconciliation. If retained, determine a normalized durable benefit from filed program terms and subsequent receipts and rerun all scenarios with only that normalized amount.

audit_findings.title: A potentially material antitrust claim is absent from both OE and the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $373.476 million accrued current liability, equal to $3.28 per valuation share, 5.3% of base value and 66.7% of the $559.759 million cash bridge; second case alleges approximately $29 million of lost profits, partly subject to trebling, plus interest, fees and costs
audit_findings.mechanism: The primary judgment is a claim ahead of common equity that arose after the FY2024 OE anchor and was not deducted in the bridge. Post-judgment interest also reduces current OE. The second case remains an unaccrued contingent claim.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has not recorded any liability for this matter as it does not believe a loss is probable, and it cannot estimate any reasonably possible loss or range of possible loss.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing converts the primary matter from an unresolved possibility into a demonstrated omission: a jury verdict was entered, the judgment was trebled, the post-trial motion was denied, and CMC recorded a $373.476 million liability. Because the anchor predates the litigation expense and the bridge omits the liability, value is overstated by $3.28 per share before considering further interest or the second case. The appeal may reverse or reduce the judgment, but that uncertainty does not eliminate the recorded claim.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the filed $373.476 million liability from the equity bridge or rebuild OE and the bridge consistently after payment; update post-judgment interest each period and separately model the second case when a filed accrual, verdict or settlement establishes its amount.

audit_findings.title: One-time NMTC settlement revenue may remain in the OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.7 million pretax, equal to 1.45% of anchor OE; conservative full-dollar OE sensitivity is approximately $94.1 million or $0.83 per share, 1.3% of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: The nonrecurring revenue increases FY2024 earnings and, if unadjusted, is projected through the operating DCF and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: In July 2024, the Exercise Period on Twain Investment Fund 249 ended, and the corresponding $ 6.7 million USBCDC capital contribution was recognized in net sales in the consolidated statement of earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The $6.7 million recognition was demonstrably nonrecurring, but its inclusion in adjusted OE is unresolved. Even conservatively treating every pretax dollar as an OE dollar and applying the supplied base operating-value-to-anchor multiple produces only about $0.83 per share, insufficient to change the valuation conclusion relative to the $62.05 base value, $68.72 bull value and $70.28 price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the NMTC settlement through the FY2024 OE reconciliation and remove it if retained; document the adjustment, but no conclusion-level rerun is required unless additional similar items are identified.

audit_findings.title: BRP investment gains may be projected without matching the associated compensation claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.5 million FY2024 holding gain, equal to 1.84% of anchor OE; conservative full-dollar OE sensitivity is approximately $119.4 million or $1.05 per share, 1.7% of base value; filed trust assets of $67.0 million exceeded the $48.8 million BRP liability by $18.2 million, or $0.16 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining volatile trust-asset gains in OE while excluding the associated BRP economics would inflate recurring OE. Bridge treatment affects value only if the trust assets and compensation liability are not handled as a matched pair.
audit_findings.evidence: The net holding gain on these segregated assets was $ 8.5 million in 2024, compared to a net holding gain of $ 5.0 million and a net holding loss of $ 7.1 million in 2023 and 2022, respectively, and was included in net sales in the Company's consolidated statements of earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the gain was purged is unresolved, but the filed scale is not conclusion-changing. Even a conservative full removal from OE changes base value by only about $1.05 per share. The bridge currently excludes both the trust assets and BRP liability, while the filed net asset difference is only $0.16 per share. Matching BRP expense may further reduce the actual numerator effect.
audit_findings.action: Verify that BRP holding gains and losses are excluded from normalized OE and confirm that trust assets and the BRP liability remain paired in the bridge; rerun only if tracing identifies materially larger cumulative unmatched amounts.
